messages:

Subject: Runway assessment & contingency asks for October QBR

Team + Claire,

Ahead of the QBR (week of Oct 12) I did a pass across product/engineering timelines and compiled a short "runway" assessment focused on the Acorn Health launch window. Attached: roadmap-slides-v3.pdf (high-level milestones), launch-risk-matrix.xlsx (current risk register), and a canary-runbook.md draft.

Top-level summary:
- Core model integration is on track for the soft launch date (Oct 28) but we have a 2-week buffer risk around quantization/time-to-integrate on the dedicated pool.
- End-to-end perf tests show token throughput within SLA for baseline loads but KV-cache warmup causes higher tail latency in the first 10% of requests.
- Billing instrumentation gaps remain for burst pricing scenarios (impacting customer cost estimates).

Asks for this thread: please highlight a single critical mitigation per owner and any blockers that must be escalated to leadership for the QBR deck. Claire — anything from Acorn’s side we should factor in (hard blackout dates, compliance gating)?

Suggested owners:
- Marcus: quantify the quantization/integration delta and proposed mitigation (need additional SRE time? immediate rollback plan?)
- Stephanie: finalize cost instrumentation and confirm billing metric parity for the partner contract
- Hannah: compile product-side acceptance criteria for the canary plan

I'll collate inputs by EOD Thursday so we have material for the leadership readout.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: roadmap-slides-v3.pdf (application/pdf), launch-risk-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), canary-runbook.md (text)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway assessment & contingency asks for October QBR

Lauren — quick technical update and proposed mitigation.

Status snapshot (engineering):
- Quantization: We’ve completed FP32 -> int8 model pass for the primary generator. Perf delta on dev hardware: 18% CPU/GPU speedup, but we observed a 7% decrease in a small subset of long-tail prompts (mostly long-context medical records).
- Integration delta: The dedicated pool config requires a kernel fallback for the medical-model variant; that work is ~60% done. Remaining work is two kernel-compatibility tests and a regression sweep across 3 synthetic sequences. ETA: Oct 14 if we keep current staffing.
- KV-cache tail latency: root cause appears to be cold-warm cache eviction policy on longer contexts; mitigation: increase warm-up prefetching on new sessions + 5% reserved cache capacity for first 30s.

Critical mitigation (owner: Marcus):
- Option A (preferred): Add a short-term eng burst (2 FTE SRE/infra for 8 days) to finish kernel compat and run an extended regression. This keeps Oct 28 date with lower risk.
- Option B (fallback): Push hard-launch to Nov 11 and run a canary on Oct 28 for a controlled audience.

Blockers:
- Need approval for temporary SRE allocation (budget ~2.5k/day for contractor seats) OR agreement to accept a Nov 11 hard-launch date.

I’ll attach the regression plan and perf runs in a follow-up.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Dalton <claire@acornhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Runway assessment & contingency asks for October QBR

Lauren / Marcus — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of notes from Acorn: 

- We have regulatory freeze windows in the evenings of Oct 25–29 for our clinical release cadence; that makes final-migration nights trickier. If you plan to do the hard launch Oct 28, the canary must be earlier and isolated to non-production patient flows.
- Cost sensitivity: our procurement team requires an estimate for worst-case burst spending for the first 30 days. Please include the burst scenario in the deck or we will need a holdback clause.

If Option A allows you to keep Oct 28 for a limited pilot (and not a full production flip), we can proceed. Option B (Nov 11) would force us to reschedule internal comms and is less desirable.

Happy to join a short tech check on Oct 8 if that helps.

— Claire
Claire Dalton
Director of Digital Programs
Acorn Health
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway assessment & contingency asks for October QBR

Thanks — clear thread. High level direction from leadership: we should aim for the Oct 28 limited pilot (Option A) provided we have explicit acceptance criteria and leadership approval on the contingency budget for the SRE burst. Please prepare the following for the QBR deck: 

1) A 1-slide risk ladder summarizing probability/impact and the chosen mitigation per risk owner.
2) Cost delta for the SRE burst and an explicit fallback plan if the regression shows regressions on the long-tail prompts.
3) Canary plan with stop criteria and rollback steps (Hannah).
4) A short note for Acorn about blackout windows and how the pilot will be isolated.

I will sign-off on the temporary SRE spend up to $25k as a one-time contingency if the engineering leads confirm the burst reduces launch risk materially. Marcus/Stephanie — get me the numbers by EOD Friday so we can include them in the leadership packet.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product
